plan: dispatch://INFRA-589/artifact/plan-md (v1). Summary: commit the archive (dispatch://INFRA-589/artifact/repro-harness-tar-gz) as packages/envoy/loadtest/, a Go main package `loadgen` (proxy, seed, run, tables) in the envoy module plus stack.sh (setup/start/seed/stop/status), run-step.sh (the one step command) and run-series.sh (0.25x..10x), README.md, a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry and one packages/envoy/AGENTS.md row. No Dispatch/listener/outbox code changes. Postgres 16.2+pgvector from pgserver==0.1.4 in a uv venv (CPython 3.12) with track_commit_timestamp=on and unix_socket_directories=''; nats-server via `GOBIN=$LOADTEST_ROOT/bin go install github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2@<go.mod version>`; Dispatch, listener and loadgen built from LOADTEST_SRC; everything under LOADTEST_ROOT (default ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dispatch-loadtest), started with env -i, stopped by pidfile PID. Each step resets: database recreated from template dispatch_seed, fresh NATS store, listener and Dispatch restarted. Seed records root comment ids and the spec name (spec.md), bakes routes, waits for the outbox to drain, vacuum analyzes, installs loadtest.event_commits + AFTER INSERT trigger on events, records seed.meta.json. Five write kinds (comment, anchored, reply, edit, upload); default event mix production-2026-10-26 (comment=3,anchored=33,reply=35,edit=22,upload=7), preset report-2026-10-27 (50/30/20). Route mix from a file (`<weight> <caller> <person|agent> GET <template>`, placeholders {key} {project} {artifact_id} {key_ref}), default routes-2026-10-26-1719Z.txt. Delivery per (event, session) receipt from arrival (httptrace WroteRequest) and from commit (pg_xact_commit_timestamp of the trigger row); committed counted from the database. Fixed RNG seed. Lock probe from +20 s to window end; CPU profile over the whole window; goroutine dump and heap at window end. Guard: endpoints and random tokens from stack.json, foreign endpoints refused unless -allow-foreign, NATS server_name/Dispatch token/listener token checked before the first write.

findings.finding: Per-step reset breaks the archive's saved revision tokens (seed.revs.json); seed.json lacks comment ids and the document name; seed copy may carry unpublished events; routes PATCHed every step.
findings.answer: Revision tokens reset with the database (start at r0, resync on a lost response); seed.json records anchored and plain root comment ids and spec.md; seed waits for published_at not null everywhere then vacuum analyze; routes baked into the seed template.

findings.finding: 'The same tables the report shows' has two readings (same shapes vs same numbers); 0.25x/0.5x sessions differ (spec 100/200 vs report 350/367); report never reset; delivery columns differ; step must also fix SSE, human share, mix, timing.
findings.answer: Same table shapes with the spec's columns and new numbers; piecewise-linear sessions through the spec's points (100, 200, 400, 467, 667, 1000); SSE max(1, round(req/30)), human 0.1, 30/180/20 s; a 'Differences from the root report' section lists every difference; the report-2026-10-27 preset gives the comparable 1x row.

findings.finding: 'Reproduces the first knee' has no threshold; lock table not in the column list; lock sampler window cut by short steps; main may get the lock fix first.
findings.answer: Pass = commit_order_lock.held_fraction > 0.5 at step-1x with waiters p50 > 0 and committed < offered; lock table is a required table; probe runs from +20 s to the window's end; tester runs on the PR head (Dispatch = its main base, commit in meta.json) and, if INFRA-591's fix is on main, also on the last main commit before it.

findings.finding: Arrival via WroteRequest is faithful; timed-out-but-committed writes are dropped by the archive; percentile unit unstated; optional access-log cross-check.
findings.answer: Committed counted from loadtest.event_commits, not HTTP status; expected deliveries from that set; percentiles over every (event, session) receipt; client-side GetConn->GotConn wait reported separately. The access-log cross-check is not built (arrival on loopback is the request in Dispatch's socket).

findings.finding: Commit trigger works with conditions: track_commit_timestamp before first start; own schema in the seed copy; store marker from payload; several events may carry one marker; trigger runs inside the lock; cross-host clocks for INFRA-598.
findings.answer: All adopted: track_commit_timestamp in initdb config; schema loadtest in the template; trigger stores event id, type, marker; primary event = lowest id of the kind's primary type, others counted; README states the trigger cost and the one-clock requirement.

findings.finding: Default 50/30/20 mix sends no replies or uploads, which the spec lists; reply root choice matters; upload must keep anchors and token line; marker field for uploads unverified.
findings.answer: Five kinds implemented; default production-2026-10-26 mix includes replies (77% anchored roots) and uploads (GET text, bump token, POST spec.md); plan reviewer confirmed artifact.version payloads carry summary; a kind with no readable marker is reported to the architect, never dropped.

findings.finding: 'One generator' cannot be checked at merge; two readings; conflicts with 'no Python'; needs a contract with INFRA-512.
findings.answer: Raised to the architect as the plan's one decision with a recommendation; implementer checks main for INFRA-512's generator at implementation and adopts it if present, else sends INFRA-512's architect the package path, the route-mix format and the per-request record.

findings.finding: Loopback-only guard does not protect the pod's live listener on loopback; generator writes damage any target.
findings.answer: Endpoints and random tokens come from stack.json; foreign endpoints refused before any connection unless -allow-foreign; NATS server_name, Dispatch token and listener token verified before the first write.

findings.finding: INFRA-598's needs (remote targets, long steps, non-/proc sampling, pg_monitor, other reset, replay, plugin receipt) must be in or out of scope; driver separable from stack scripts.
findings.answer: Out of scope, listed in the plan's 'What this harness does not do'; loadgen run is separable via -allow-foreign; samples.json keeps the 5 s series.

findings.finding: Before/after across commits: an older build cannot start on a newer seed.
findings.answer: LOADTEST_SRC selects the build; seed.meta.json records the migration level; run-step.sh refuses a build older than the seed, naming both.

findings.finding: Generator caps at 4,000 in flight (5x/10x sent 133 req/s); zero rates impossible.
findings.answer: Cap raised to 25,000 (fd limit 1,048,576); tables mark a step whose sent rate is below 95% of target; 0 is a real zero.

findings.finding: Archive defects: private names in route-mix-INFRA-324.txt; hard-coded paths; separate module; obsolete patch; dump inside CPU profile window; clock seeds; postgres CPU sums every postgres on the box; unpinned pgserver; socket path limit; REPORT.md.
findings.answer: route-mix-INFRA-324.txt, build-diff.patch, REPORT.md, Python scripts not committed; LOADTEST_ROOT/LOADTEST_SRC; folded into the envoy module; dump at window end outside the profile; fixed RNG seed and counter markers; Postgres CPU from the postmaster's tree; pgserver==0.1.4 pinned; unix_socket_directories=''; check-private-names run on the package.

findings.finding: Criteria no machine can check need checks (N sessions, 2-core, one command, README columns).
findings.answer: run.log counts (N registered, N x 6 subscriptions); meta.json records nproc, CPU model, GOMAXPROCS; A2 checks the output files; README columns checked by the reviewer (a test of README text is a wording test, excluded by the repository's test rules).

findings.finding: Unsourced claims: 'same tables', 'on main reproduces', pgserver version, pod env URLs, route split inside groups, 467/667, proxy adds ~4 ms.
findings.answer: Each stated in the plan with its source or as INFERENCE: report's sessions differ; knee on main is the tester's measurement; setup prints postgres --version; pod env checked by the planner (DISPATCH_URL, ENVOY_URL, ENVOY_NATS_URL set); split inside groups marked INFERENCE; 467/667 from the spec's points; README states the proxy's measured ~4 ms.
